messages.subject: Pvalue canculation
parts:
Hello,

In my project, I have 6 bacterial strains in single replicate and I want to compare three of them (from one lineage) to others (3 strains from another lineage). In the matrix, I had specified (1/3,1/3,1/3,-1/3,-1/3,-1/3) and MSstats generated pvalues for me as well (version 3.9.0). Now I tried the same thing with the same version but it didn't generate pvalues. I am wondering if the pvalue calculation depends on another R package. I am not sure if I have updated other packages but definitely I have the MSstats version. Could you please help me with this.

Best,
Amir

messages.author: 085b00b73e467d88
messages.subject: Re: Pvalue canculation
parts: What's your experimental design in terms of Condition, BioReplicate, and Run? Based on your contrast matrix, you are considering 6 conditions. Correct? How many runs do you have per condition? How does the summarized values for one protein (e.g. I6WXK4) in all runs look like?

messages.author: 8c88e75d9eb66be4
messages.subject: Re: Pvalue canculation
parts: They are not really two different conditions. It's a very large dataset of bacterial strains with different genetic background. I am comparing three strains of one lineage with another three strains from another lineage. So I have no biological/technical replicates. I had done such an analysis before by MSstats and it produced both FC and Pvalue for me. I forgot to do one of the comparison at the time. That's why I am doing this now. However it doesn't generate pvalue anymore. That's why my matrix is like this (-1/3,-1/3,-1/3,1/3,1/3,1/3)

messages.author: 085b00b73e467d88
messages.subject: Re: Pvalue canculation
parts: You need to have replicates in order to calculate the standard error of the estimate, the t-statistic, and the p-value. This is true for MSstats and statistical inference in general.
